title: Semilocal completion comparisons and heights of formal singular boundaries
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian normal Nagata domain over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. Let $0\ne x\in R$ be a nonunit, and suppose $R$ is $(x)$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], universally catenary, not quasi-excellent, with every quotient $R/K$ for a nonzero ideal $K$ quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. For each finite extension $L/\operatorname{Frac}R$, let $B_L$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume that $B_L$ is finite as an $R$-module, normal, Nagata, universally catenary and $(x)$-adically complete, that $B_L/xB_L$ is quasi-excellent, and that the maximal-ideal completion $\widehat{(B_L)_{\mathfrak n}}$ is a normal local domain for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B_L$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

For each such $L,\mathfrak n$, put $C_{L,\mathfrak n}=\varprojlim_j (B_L)_{\mathfrak n}/x^j(B_L)_{\mathfrak n}$. For a Noetherian ring $T$, write $\operatorname{Sing}(T)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}T:T_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is not regular local}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-regular-scheme]. A minimal singular prime is a member of this set containing no strictly smaller member. Define
$$\mathcal S=\{(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s):\mathfrak s\text{ is a minimal singular prime of }C_{L,\mathfrak n},\ \mathfrak s\cap B_L=(0)\}.$$
Height means $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=\dim T_{\mathfrak p}$, with Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume $\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$, let $h=\min\{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak s:(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s)\in\mathcal S\}\geq2$, and fix a triple $(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s)\in\mathcal S$ of height $h$. Put $B=B_L$. For any finite set $\gamma$ of maximal ideals of $B$ containing $\mathfrak n$, put $S_\gamma=B\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak a\in\gamma}\mathfrak a$, $B_\gamma=S_\gamma^{-1}B$, $D_\gamma=\varprojlim_j B_\gamma/x^jB_\gamma$, and let $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak s$ under the canonical map $D_\gamma\to C_{L,\mathfrak n}$.
Then $D_\gamma$ is Noetherian, normal, Nagata, universally catenary and a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The map $B\to D_\gamma$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and its reduction is the canonical isomorphism $B_\gamma/xB_\gamma\simeq D_\gamma/xD_\gamma$. The prime $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ contracts to zero in $B$, has height $h$, and $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}$ is not regular local. Let $E_\gamma$ be the integral closure of the domain $D_\gamma/\mathfrak s_\gamma$ in its fraction field and put
$$\Delta_\gamma(x)=\{\mathfrak Q\cap B:\mathfrak Q\text{ is a prime minimal over }xE_\gamma\}.$$
This is also the set of contractions to $B$ of the primes of $D_\gamma$ minimal over $\mathfrak s_\gamma+xD_\gamma$. Every $\mathfrak Q\in\Delta_\gamma(x)$ has height $h+1$ in $B$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, Claim 5.4, (5.8)–(5.11), printed pp.12–13; description of Delta before Claim 5.4; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height] to the underlying commutative ring $R$, keeping $x$, every extension $L/\operatorname{Frac}R$, the rings $B_L$, and the chosen $(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s)$ and $\gamma$ unchanged. Its hypotheses are precisely ours with the additional requirement that $R$ be a $\mathbf Q$-algebra omitted. In particular the family $\mathcal S$, its minimum $h$, and the chosen height-minimizing triple are the same: their definitions use only the underlying rings, localizations, completions, and regularity. The definitions of $S_\gamma,B_\gamma,D_\gamma,\mathfrak s_\gamma,E_\gamma$ and $\Delta_\gamma(x)$ are also identical. The cited statement therefore gives all five properties of $D_\gamma$, flatness and the reduction isomorphism, contraction zero, height $h$ and nonregularity of $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}$, the equality of the two descriptions of $\Delta_\gamma(x)$, and height $h+1$ of every member of that set. This is exactly the required conclusion.
